summary.oneLiner: Revenue declined YoY due to timing of large Mexico project billing and Africa project delay, but order book remains robust at INR5,354cr with strong visibility in ZLD, CBG, and nuclear desalination; margin guidance revised slightly down to 15-16% as CBG and new membrane tech scale up, positioning the company for 20% long-term growth.

one-line thesis: Revenue declined YoY due to timing of large Mexico project billing and Africa project delay, but order book remains robust at INR5,354cr with strong visibility in ZLD, CBG, and nuclear desalination; margin guidance revised slightly down to 15-16% as CBG and new membrane tech scale up, positioning the company for 20% long-term growth.
financial scorecard: Revenue: -23% YoY (INR1,248cr vs INR1,619cr) due to Mexico project timing; EBITDA: -72% YoY (INR77cr vs INR273cr) due to higher costs and project delay; PAT: -71% YoY (INR45cr vs INR189cr); order book: INR5,354cr (+flat YoY); net debt: no net debt mentioned, but forex gains offset prior losses, USD-denominated orders now hedged on cash flow crystallization
guidance: Revenue growth: revised to 12-15% for FY26 (from 18-20%); EBITDA margin: 15-16% (down 1ppt from prior 16-17%); order inflow: INR2,700cr in advanced discussions; capex/commissioning: CBG projects commencing Q3FY26, 2-3 projects expected to contribute INR45cr revenue in next two quarters
order book & pipeline: INR5,354cr as of Sep 30, 2025; 53% ZLD, 15% CBG, 32% O&M/spares; INR2,700cr in advanced discussions; L1 for INR400cr nuclear seawater desalination tender (expected order by Dec 2025)
segment / subsidiary detail: ZLD: core business, 53% of order book; CBG: new vertical, 15% of order book, 2-3 projects commencing Q3FY26 with INR45cr revenue expected in next two quarters; O&M/spares: growing to target 40-45% of revenue, boosted by Mexico and India project handovers; REM membrane: revolutionary new product for raw effluent treatment, trials underway in textile/paper/F&B; carbon capture: pilot in Q4FY26, commercial revenue expected H2FY27
growth verticals / optionality: CBG scaling to 3-5 industrial projects/year; REM membrane penetration in high-volume sectors (textile, paper, F&B); nuclear desalination tender conversion; carbon capture commercialization; technology licensing and contract manufacturing deals in advanced stages
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin guidance revised to 15-16% due to higher leadership/expansion costs and Africa project delay; CBG margins expected to start at 14-15% and scale to 18-20% with volume; REM membrane reduces chemical/sludge costs by 30-50%, improving OPEX; cost advantage over global players: 10-15% lower capex, 50% lower OPEX in ZLD
capex / expansion: Capex funded via IPO proceeds; focus on scaling CBG production and REM membrane manufacturing; no specific capex number disclosed, but investments aligned to reach INR1,300-1,400cr revenue capacity by FY28-29
capital allocation: IPO proceeds allocated to capacity expansion (CBG, REM), R&D, and technology licensing; focus on high-margin O&M/spares (target 40-45% of revenue); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; licensing deals expected to generate non-operating top-line
risks & watch-items: Project execution delays (e.g., Africa approvals); forex volatility on legacy USD/peso exposure (now largely hedged); regulatory uncertainty in emerging markets; CBG feedstock dependency on client waste availability; competition from global membrane players
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but emphasizes strong order book, technological leadership, and long-term 20% growth trajectory; highlights innovation (REM, CBG, carbon capture) as key differentiators; tone is proactive on scaling and margin expansion
non-obvious takeaways: CBG projects leverage existing industrial waste streams (negative cost input), eliminating feedstock risk; REM membrane enables direct raw effluent treatment, reducing footprint and CAPEX by 30-40%; nuclear desalination L1 win is a high-barrier entry into government infrastructure; Sharjah entity remains tax-free on exports, boosting effective tax rate to only 12-14%

themes.title: Water & environmental-infra EPC
themes.need: AMRUT, Namami Gange and Jal Jeevan still define the pipeline, but Q1FY27 put a number on the funding freeze. WPIL's consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 501cr while STANDALONE collapsed 37% to INR 115cr as domestic Jal Jeevan invoicing froze, with INR 300-350cr of JJM receivables pending (mostly West Bengal, some MP) and nil received in the quarter - management expects substantial inflow only in Q2/H2. The offsetting discovery is that the theme has quietly become international: WPIL's overseas revenue roughly doubled to INR 386cr, about 77% of consolidated, on PCI Africa's first full execution quarter plus Gruppo Aturia MENA demand, lifting consolidated EBITDA margin to 15.04%. EIEL carries an all-time-high order book (~6x revenue); WABAG on desalination/technology; JISLJALEQS/JISLDVREQS and MAHEPC add micro-irrigation and water-efficiency equipment; EMSLIMITED/SPMLINFRA/JASH/DENTA/ELECTCAST/AWHCL add sewerage, control equipment and ductile-iron piping. Execution conversion, not order intake, remains the binding constraint.
themes.driver: JJM/AMRUT fund releases unlocking billing (WPIL's INR 300-350cr receivable is the tracer); FY27 order inflow; desalination + NTPC BESS EPC ramp; international Africa/MENA execution.
